Package com.im.njams.sdk.communication

Class TransportNotApplicableException

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.lang.Throwable
      • java.lang.Exception
        • java.lang.RuntimeException
          • com.im.njams.sdk.communication.TransportNotApplicableException
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable
    public class TransportNotApplicableException
extends RuntimeException
    Thrown by a transport implementation from its initialization to state that it is not applicable in the current environment, e.g. because a library it requires is not present. This is an expected outcome rather than an error: the SDK skips such an implementation and looks for another one.

    • Method Detail

      • isNotApplicable

        public static boolean isNotApplicable​(Throwable failure)
        Whether the given failure says that a transport implementation is not applicable on this classpath rather than broken. Two things say so, and both must name a type of one of the two JMS APIs: a failed cast, which is what a connection factory of the other JMS namespace produces, and a missing type. The whole cause chain is examined, because an implementation may wrap the failure into an exception of its own.

        Deliberately narrow in both directions: a type that is missing for any other reason, such as a broker client library that was not deployed, is a real error, and so is a failed cast anywhere else — this classification is applied to every transport's providers, not only to the JMS ones.

        Parameters:
        failure - the failure to classify.
        Returns:
        whether the failure means "not applicable here" rather than "broken".
